newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Franco says forex policy unchanged - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Franco says forex policy unchanged - paper.

text.p: Central Bank director Gustavo Franco said Monday's surprising 0.28 percent decline in Brazil's foreign exchange mini-band did not signal a new exchange rate policy, Gazeta Mercantil reported.

Responding to market speculation that the Central Bank opted for a larger-than-normal mini-depreciation to improve trade accounts, Franco told the paper: "We are not going to increase our exports with a foreign exchange correction or subsidy.
"A large part of our imports are going to help productivity and should lead to greater exports," Franco told an audience in Barcelona at the Inter-American Development Bank's annual meeting.

The Central Bank usually depreciates its mini-band, in which the real currency trades against the dollar, by between 0.10 percent and 0.15 percent, four to six times a month. The policy results in roughly a 0.60 percent devaluation over the month.
Monday's 0.28 percent decline was the biggest single drop in the mini-band since March 1996, Gazeta said. So far in March, the mini-band has been depreciated 0.55 percent.

Although the Central Bank never explains its actions, analysts speculated that Monday's large drop may have been made to keep to its usual depreciation pace to achieve the standard 0.60 percent depreciation by the end of the month.
They also said the bank may be trying to encourage soy exporters to carry out foreign exchange transactions before the end of the month.
